add.issue.name: 01 Test environment isolation: npm test green in any agent session

edit.description.md:
# 01: Test environment isolation — `npm test` green in any agent session

**Implement:** coder
**Effort:** lo

**What to build:** the repo's unit gate (`npm test` = prettier check + vitest
with the two e2e suites excluded) passes in any agent session, including
shells where the host injects git config through environment variables
(`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_i` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_i`, e.g. an
agent's push guard). A fixture that pushes into a bare remote must never be
intercepted by a host hook, no matter what the surrounding environment
carries.

**Blocked by:** None (can start immediately). Every later ticket's green gate
depends on this one.

**Status:** ready-for-agent

**Mechanism (planner-verified in this run — implement exactly this, not the
audit's original shape):** every git child process the codebase spawns
receives a module-load-time snapshot of `process.env` — the exported `gitEnv`
object in `source/git/git-utils.ts` (line 89), passed as the spawn `env`
(lines 127 and 251). Clearing `process.env` in any test hook (what
`useTempHome` does for `HOME`) cannot reach those children, and twelve test
files drive git children without calling `useTempHome` at all. So the fix
strips the keys **from the `gitEnv` object itself**, from a new vitest setup
file. Test-side only: no production code, nothing in the published package.

**Files in scope:**

- NEW `source/test/setup/git-env-isolated.ts`
- `vitest.config.ts` — register the new file first in `setupFiles`
- nothing else. Do not touch `source/test/helpers/git-repo.ts` or
  `source/git/git-utils.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] The setup file imports the `gitEnv` object and deletes every key
      starting with `GIT_CONFIG_` at module scope, with a short comment
      explaining why (env-injected config is captured in the snapshot before
      any test runs; fixtures must push without tripping host hooks).
- [ ] `vitest.config.ts` lists it first in `setupFiles` (before
      `no-git-outside-tmp.ts`).
- [ ] `git status` clean; the diff touches exactly those two files.

**Proof (all must exit 0 in the ticket worktree):**

```bash
# simulate the host guard: a hooks dir whose pre-push fails every push
mkdir -p /tmp/guard && printf '#!/bin/sh\necho guard\nexit 1\n' > /tmp/guard/pre-push && chmod +x /tmp/guard/pre-push
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/tmp/guard npm test
npm test          # still green with a clean environment
npx tsc --noEmit
```

Before the fix, the first command fails (the planner reproduced it:
`source/test/git-pull.test.ts` 2/3 red with the guard message; full suite
66 red tests). After the fix the planner saw the full suite green under the
simulated guard: 186 files, 2246 tests, exit 0.

add.issue.name: 02 Tree hygiene + npm package fix (untrack .ome/project.json, publishConfig, git install builds dist)

edit.description.md:
# 02: Tree hygiene + npm package fix (B1, B3-code, n2, n3)

**Implement:** agent
**Effort:** med

**What to build:** a clean public tree and a publish-ready package. The
operator's project descriptor leaves the tree and can never be re-committed;
`package.json` carries no non-standard key and states its access explicitly;
and a git install actually works — `npm i -g git+https://github.com/T-Crypt/oh-my-epiq.git`
builds the bins when `dist/` is missing instead of silently shipping a
package with no `dist/` (today `prepare` only runs husky, while the build
lives on `prepack`, which git installs never trigger).

**Blocked by:** 01 (the green gate must be trustworthy in this session)

**Status:** ready-for-agent

**Changes:**

- `git rm --cached .ome/project.json`, then add `.ome/project.json` to
  `.gitignore` (keep the existing `.ome/events/` and `.ome/log/` lines; do not
  blanket-ignore `.ome/`). (B1)
- Delete the non-standard top-level `allowScripts` key from `package.json`.
  It is ignored by npm; if it turns out to matter to local tooling, say so in
  the PR description instead of keeping the key. (n2)
- Add `"publishConfig": {"access": "public"}`. (n3)
- Close the `prepare`/`prepack` gap (B3): `prepare` keeps installing the husky
  hooks **and** builds `dist/` when it is missing. Shape: `prepare` runs a new
  small script (`source/scripts/prepare.mjs` is a fine home) that checks for
  the built outputs (`dist/index.js` and `dist/mcp.js`); when both are
  present it does nothing (local clones stay fast), when either is missing it
  runs the same build `build:npm` runs. Verify the husky hooks still activate
  on a fresh clone (commit-msg and pre-push both tracked under `.husky/`).
  The registry tarball path is untouched: `prepack` still does the full build.

**Files in scope:** `.gitignore`, `package.json`, `.ome/project.json`
(untrack only), new `source/scripts/prepare.mjs`, and only if the script must
reuse a build helper: at most one existing `source/scripts/*.mjs` (prefer a
standalone script over touching shared build code).

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] `git ls-files .ome/` is empty; `.gitignore` lists `.ome/project.json`.
- [ ] `package.json`: no `allowScripts`, has `publishConfig.access`, and
      `prepare` = husky + build-when-missing.
- [ ] `npm pack --dry-run` manifest keeps its shape: `LICENSE`, `README.md`,
      `package.json` plus everything under `dist/` (413 files at 1.13.0) —
      no `source/`, no `docs/`, no `.ome/`.
- [ ] `npm test` green in the worktree.

**Proof (in the ticket worktree, all must succeed):**

```bash
# the git-install path, locally: fresh clone of this branch, clean install
git clone file://$PWD /tmp/ome-clone && cd /tmp/ome-clone
rm -rf node_modules dist
npm install            # prepare must build dist/ from scratch
npm i -g .             # then the bins work
ome --version
which ome ome-mcp
```

(`ome --version` is the README's own verification command; the real
`git+https://` form can only be proven after the repo is public and this PR
is merged.)

edit.description.md:
# 03: README — unslop + precision

**Implement:** writer
**Effort:** med

**What to build:** the #1 public surface, made true. The README is unsloped
and precise: a stranger who reads it can run every command in it and see it
work, and every number, URL, and capability claim in it is checkable against
the code. This lands after ticket 02 so the Install section documents
install behavior that actually exists.

**Blocked by:** 02 (docs must match the fixed install behavior)

**Status:** ready-for-agent

**Before writing:** read `/home/tcrypt/.agents/skills/unslop/SKILL.md` and
apply it to the whole file. Precision edits below are on top of the unslop
pass, not instead of it.

**Changes (all in `README.md`):**

- **Install section — rewrite** (the current text says "not published to npm
  yet" and warns the `git+…` install is broken; both are false after the
  release):
  - primary: `npm i -g oh-my-epiq` (bins `ome`, `ome-mcp`),
  - ad-hoc: `npx -p oh-my-epiq ome gui`,
  - secondary: `npm i -g git+https://github.com/T-Crypt/oh-my-epiq.git`
    (works: install builds `dist/` when missing) and the packed-tarball path,
  - one line for the binary installer: `curl -fsSL
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/T-Crypt/oh-my-epiq/main/install.sh | sh`
    (m2) — prebuilt single binary, `OME_VERSION` pins a tag,
  - keep `ome --version` as the verify step.
  - **Never document `npx ome`** — that npm name belongs to an unrelated
    package.
- **M2:** "23 bundled palettes" → the true count. Recount the shipped `THEMES`
  record in `source/gui/client/lib/theme.ts` at write time (it was 22 in the
  audit; say the number only if it still matches, otherwise drop the number).
- **M5:** the MCP pitch says "every write takes a full id, a 7-char `ref` or
  a name" — resolution is id-or-ref only (title/name never resolves; the
  resolver and the tool description say so). Reword: tickets by full id or
  7-char ref; tags by name; assignees by id.
- **n1:** the closing line "Never leave your editor." is from the
  single-TUI era; the product has four faces including a phone app. Replace
  with a line that fits, or drop it.

**Files in scope:** `README.md` only.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] No sentence in the file is false for a stranger running it: every
      command, URL, port, code lifetime, and count verified against the
      post-02 tree (npm name and bins from `package.json`; the port, pairing
      code, cookie and `OME_MCP_FULL` facts were already checked clean in the
      audit — re-verify only what the rewrite touches).
- [ ] The Install section names `oh-my-epiq`, not "not published yet".
- [ ] `npx ome` appears nowhere in the file.
- [ ] Unchanged sections keep their content (Batteries included, Roadmap,
      Remote and mobile, Coming from Epiq, Credit) — the Credit section and
      all `ljtn/epiq` attribution stay intact.
- [ ] `npm test` green in the worktree.

**Proof:** in the ticket worktree:

```bash
npm test
rg -n "npx ome" README.md   # no output
rg -n "not published" README.md   # no output
```

plus the writer's claim-by-claim table in the PR description (claim → where
it's true in the tree).

add.issue.name: 04 Docs and shipped skill alignment (AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, skills/ome/SKILL.md)

edit.description.md:
# 04: Docs and shipped skill alignment (M1, m5, m4, n4)

**Implement:** agent
**Effort:** lo

**What to build:** the docs an agent or an outside contributor reads tell the
truth: no command that fetches a foreign package, the unit-suite wording
matches the repo's real gate, the push-hook trap is documented, and the
shipped skill stops mandating one vendor's remote workflow.

**Blocked by:** 01 (its green gate runs in an agent session)

**Status:** ready-for-agent

**Changes:**

- **M1 — `AGENTS.md:43`:** `npx ome gui` → `ome gui` (after install), with
  `npx -p oh-my-epiq ome gui` as the no-install form. The npm name `ome`
  belongs to an unrelated package, so `npx ome` must not survive anywhere in
  the tracked tree.
- **m5 — `AGENTS.md` build section:** "`npx vitest run` for the unit suite"
  pulls in the docker/browser e2e suites. Align it with the repo's actual unit
  definition as CONTRIBUTING.md states it: `npm test` (prettier check plus
  vitest excluding `source/test/e2e/**` and `source/test/e2e-collab/**`).
- **m4 — `CONTRIBUTING.md`:** the pre-push hook runs the full gate including
  the container suite, which needs the local docker image. Add a line to the
  "Before you open a pull request" section: build the e2e image once before
  your first push (`npm run build:e2e:image`) or the push hook fails with a
  docker "image not found".
- **n4 — `skills/ome/SKILL.md` (default: SOFTEN):** the final bullets mandate
  GitHub-specific integration ("gh pr merge --rebase, never --merge") and
  Claude-specific commit hygiene inside a git-agnostic product. Rewrite them
  remote- and harness-agnostic, keeping the substance:
  - rebase onto the target before integrating; integrate with a rebase-merge
    where the remote supports one (GitHub: `gh pr merge --rebase`), so the
    main line stays a flat sequence of ref-prefixed commits — that flatness
    is what commit↔ticket linking reads; a merge commit buries the branch,
  - the authorship rule keeps its meaning (the repo's configured git user is
    the sole author; no tool/model attribution lines or generated footers in
    commits) phrased for any harness.
- **Regenerate, never hand-edit:** `source/mcp/skill-content.ts` is generated
  from the skill file by `npm run build:npm`; run it after editing the skill.
  A unit test fails when the committed copy lags, which is the safety net —
  let it run.

**Files in scope:** `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`,
`skills/ome/SKILL.md`, `source/mcp/skill-content.ts` (generated output of
`npm run build:npm` — expect it in the diff, never edit it by hand).

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Zero tracked occurrences of `npx ome` (AGENTS.md:43 was the only one in
      the tree at audit time).
- [ ] AGENTS.md's test instruction names `npm test` (or the exact exclude
      command CONTRIBUTING.md uses) and its GUI line no longer says `npx ome`.
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md warns about the e2e docker image before the first push.
- [ ] The skill's merge/authorship bullets name no vendor; `source/mcp/skill-content.ts`
      is the regenerated copy of the edited skill.
- [ ] `npm test` green (includes the skill-content lag test).

**Proof:** in the ticket worktree:

```bash
npm run build:npm && git status --short   # only the intended files differ
npm test
rg -n "npx ome" AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md skills/ome/SKILL.md README.md   # no output
```

add.issue.name: 05 Release 1.14.0: version bump, RELEASE_NOTES.md, local tag v1.14.0 (unpushed)

edit.description.md:
# 05: Release 1.14.0 — version, notes, local tag (do not push)

**Implement:** agent
**Effort:** lo

**What to build:** the release artifact, staged and unpushed: the package at
version 1.14.0, the release notes in the repo, and the annotated tag
`v1.14.0` on the release commit — ready for the router's confirmation gate
(visibility flip → tag push → release notes attached → npm publish). This
ticket publishes nothing: the tag stays local, no GitHub Release exists yet
(CI creates it **on the tag push** — that push is the publish event, per the
audit's M4).

**Blocked by:** 02, 03, 04 (the release must be cut from the tree where all
findings have landed; the router merges those first)

**Status:** ready-for-agent

**Changes (in the ticket worktree, off the post-04 `origin/main`):**

- Bump `package.json` `version` to `1.14.0` — the only field changed.
- `npm run build:npm` — regenerates `source/version.ts` (1.14.0) and
  `source/mcp/skill-content.ts` (byte-identical if 04 landed; expect no
  drift). Both are generated files: never hand-edit.
- New `RELEASE_NOTES.md` at the repo root. Content: **Oh-My-Epiq 1.14.0 —
  first public release.** What OME is over Epiq (same engine and event model;
  four faces: CLI, TUI, browser board, agent MCP; Epiq migration; Oh-My-Pocket
  look including the phone app; the pruned agent MCP with `OME_MCP_FULL`
  opt-in). Install paths, exactly as the post-03 README states them:
  `npm i -g oh-my-epiq`, `npx -p oh-my-epiq ome gui`, `npm i -g
  git+https://github.com/T-Crypt/oh-my-epiq.git`, and the `install.sh`
  binary one-liner. Attribution: hard fork of Epiq by Jonatan Lampa (@ljtn),
  MIT, look follows Pi Pocket / Oh-My-Pocket. Keep it scannable, no slogans.
- Annotated tag `v1.14.0` on the release commit
  (`git tag -a v1.14.0 -m "$(cat RELEASE_NOTES.md)"`), so the notes live in
  git history with the tag. Note what this does **not** do: the GitHub
  Release that CI creates on the tag push will have an **empty body**.
  Verified against the action CI uses (`softprops/action-gh-release` v2,
  `src/github.ts` + `src/util.ts`): it takes the release body only from its
  `body`/`body_path` inputs, which `ci.yml` never sets, and the annotated
  tag's message is never read. The notes therefore reach the release at the
  gate: the router runs `gh release edit v1.14.0` with `RELEASE_NOTES.md`
  after CI finishes (spec's gate checklist).
- **Do not push the tag. Do not publish to npm. Do not change repo
  visibility.** All three are the router's gate actions.

**Files in scope:** `package.json`, `RELEASE_NOTES.md` (new),
`source/version.ts` (generated), local tag `v1.14.0`.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] `package.json` at `1.14.0`; `source/version.ts` says the same (check
      after `npm run build:npm`, not by hand-editing).
- [ ] `RELEASE_NOTES.md` exists at the repo root and its text is the tag
      message.
- [ ] `v1.14.0` exists locally and is annotated: `git cat-file -t v1.14.0`
      prints `tag` (a `commit` would be a lightweight tag — reject it).
- [ ] The PR description says plainly: the release body is attached by the
      router at the gate (`gh release edit`), because CI's release action is
      never given a notes file.
- [ ] `npm pack --dry-run` names `oh-my-epiq-1.14.0.tgz` and lists only
      `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `package.json` plus `dist/**` — no `source/`,
      no `docs/`, no `.ome/`.
- [ ] `npm test` green; `git status` clean; `git ls-remote --tags origin
      v1.14.0` returns nothing (tag not pushed).
- [ ] The 56 inherited upstream tags are untouched: `git tag -l` shows only
      `v1.14.0` added.

**Proof (in the ticket worktree):**

```bash
npm run build:npm && npm test
rg -n '"version"' package.json            # 1.14.0
rg -n "1\.14\.0" source/version.ts
git tag -l v1.14.0 && git cat-file -t v1.14.0     # v1.14.0 / tag
git for-each-ref refs/tags/v1.14.0 --format='%(contents:subject)'   # first line of the notes
npm pack --dry-run 2>&1 | sed -n '1,12p'          # oh-my-epiq-1.14.0.tgz + top-level listing
git ls-remote --tags origin v1.14.0               # empty: nothing pushed
```
